title: feat(plugin-audit): seal the audit log by default and expire sealed rows by whole checkpoints (ADR-0154 D8, D10)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuWkuYc3V797qxZSYHo5QzBw)_

Part of #31908

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: `sys_audit_log` now declares `lifecycle.seal` on every deployment, so `os migrate audit-key-material`, `audit-mail-bodies`, `audit-metadata-bodies` and `audit-side-copies` with `--apply` refuse on SQLite or Turso without `--sealer-stopped`, and on Postgres or MySQL take the audit seal lock and refuse after ten minutes, where 18.6.0 ran them unlocked on a deployment that sealed nothing; `os audit verify` exits 1 on a row it reads `late` and unsealed (the S4 arm); `os audit verify` refuses with `archive_not_connected` and exits 2 where the `archive` datasource is declared and not connected on its own boot (fix: `autoConnect: true`, or make it reachable), where 18.6.0 printed that nothing is sealed and exited 0; `verifyAuditLedger` throws for `sys_audit_log` when its `archive` datasource is not connected and no `archive` is passed. This breaks the bound changeset `35c9a30` (#33675) set ("a deployment that did not opt in sees no change"). Widened: `LifecycleService.registerExpiryPrefix` and the `LifecycleExpiryPrefix*` types (the request with `tenants` and `tenantColumn`), `policy: 'expiry'`, the skip reasons `seal-expiry-pending` and `seal-delete-unsupported`.
Metadata-protocol: semantic — beside `lifecycle.seal`, the authored `retention.maxAge`, `ttl.expireAfter` and `archive.keep` no longer delete a row at its row cutoff: rows leave by whole checkpoints under a signed expiry amendment (seat ruling on review 7198128323 S2; the changeset moves all four packages `minor`)
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — this claim's second PR (amendment 7193137455) rewrites `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md`, which says the sweeper deletes sealed rows until it lands (hence `Part of`, not `Fixes`)

## 维护者速读

- 每个部署的审计日志从此默认带防篡改封印：管理员跑审计校验时，被改、被删、被脱敏、按策略到期的记录都能分辨出来，热库和归档库都算。
- **这是对运维可见的破坏性变化**：SQLite 和 Turso 部署下次跑 `os migrate audit-*`（包括升级流程里的 `audit-side-copies --apply`）会被拒，要先停掉服务再带 `--sealer-stopped`；Postgres 和 MySQL 会先等封存锁，最多等 10 分钟。
- **过期删除不可撤回**：过了保留期的审计记录按整段检查点删除，删之前先签一份到期说明，校验时读作“到期”而不是“丢失”，但删掉的行找不回来。
- **宿主没有传加密服务时**，`sys_audit_log` 过了 `archive.keep` 也会一直留着，封存器每小时报一次 error。出错时只会多留、不会多删：链条有缺口、签名不可信、检查点或到期说明不属于这条链、前后接不上，都一律保留并告警一次。
- **按租户设的保留期**只在它设在链所用的那一列上时才对这个组织的链生效；其他链（不属于任何组织的链，以及保留期设在另一列上的对象的所有链）一律按所有保留期里最长的那个保留。代价是：保留期设在非链列上的对象，租户设的更短保留期对它的封存记录不起作用，记录会留到最长的保留期。

**Tier:** Tier H (declared narrowing: the Clause-② line above; seat ruling on review 7202871622). About 2,400 changed lines (under 3,000). No governed path: `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` changes one `.describe()` sentence only, and the `skills/**` wording fix is split into this claim's second PR (amendment 7193137455), Tier H on its own. The release page `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx` is release-owned and is not edited here (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails").

## What changes

ADR-0154 D8 + D10, slice P4c, the last slice of #31908.

- **`sys_audit_log` is sealed by default.** Its lifecycle now declares `seal: { valueFields: ['old_value', 'new_value', 'metadata'] }` (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts`). The chain column is the default `tenant_id` (a lookup, one text value on every store).
- **LifecycleService: sealed objects expire only through a registered seam** (`packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts`). New public `registerExpiryPrefix(expiry)` (the name slice plan 6759503769 ruled) (one slot; a later registration replaces it; the disposer clears only its own) and the types `LifecycleExpiryPrefix`, `LifecycleExpiryPrefixRequest`, `LifecycleExpiryPrefixRun`. For an object with `lifecycle.seal`:
  - the `retention.maxAge` / `ttl.expireAfter` legs and the archive's `keep` prune never delete by a row cutoff; each asks the seam to `plan({ object, policy, policyValue, cutoff, tenants?, tenantColumn? })`;
  - each run's `rowIds` are deleted by id (hot and archive for an archiving object; through the engine, reap guards asked, for the rest), and `run.complete()` is called only when every one is gone;
  - with no seam registered, rows are kept, the archive copy still runs, the sweep reports `seal-expiry-pending`, and one `warn` says so;
  - a tenant-scoped window (on the partition `reap()` uses, through the same floors) travels as `tenants`, with the column it is set on (`tenantColumn`), which need not be the chain column (review 7202871622 S4);
  - an archive store with no `bulkDelete` is never planned (`seal-delete-unsupported`), so no amendment is signed over rows it could not delete.
- **plugin-audit: the expiry writer** (new `audit-seal/expiry.ts`, `AuditSealer.expire`, registration in `audit-plugin.ts`):
  - per chain, from the first remaining checkpoint (which must follow and link to the last admitted expiry, or be sequence 0), take consecutive checkpoints whose window ended at or before the chain's cutoff aligned down to a UTC day, each the chain's own, linked to the one before and admitted by a trusted signature, at most 10,000 rows a sweep; a chain holding a checkpoint or stored expiry that is not its own, or one that does not link, is not expired at all and is said once (review 7202871622 M3);
  - each chain's window: where `tenantColumn` is the object's chain column, an organization's chain takes its own tenant window (else the global one); every other chain, the chain of rows about no organization and every chain of an object whose windows sit on another column, takes the longest window configured; its amendment signs it (seat rulings on S1 and on review 7202871622 S4). No row is read to pick a window;
  - sign and store the chain's `expiry` amendment (the S1 key-id loop, then the sink, best-effort), then answer the run; `complete()` removes each checkpoint's seed, then the checkpoint, oldest first (review n5), and removes a seed only when it is the secret sealed under that checkpoint's own coordinate;
  - a stored, admitted amendment that still covers the first remaining checkpoint is resumed (no second amendment); the resume branch admits each checkpoint as the fresh branch does (the chain's own, linked to the one before, a trusted signature), requires them consecutive from the amendment's first sequence to its last sequence and digest, reads them a page at a time, and removes them oldest first; otherwise nothing in the range is deleted; an unadmitted amendment deletes nothing;
  - a gap or an untrusted checkpoint stops the chain there and is said once;
  - planning holds the `audit.sealer` lock and the DB seal-pass lock, so two replicas never sign two amendments over one range; a fully drained plan is memoised for the day;
  - registered only when the plugin has a crypto provider (otherwise nothing could be signed);
  - the sealer's head falls back to the last admitted expiry (the chain's own, its signature verified) when a chain has no checkpoint left (`last_sequence`, `last_removed_digest`), and the object floor to the newest admitted `covered_to`; both, like the expiry, read stored amendments page by page until an admitted one answers.
- **Verifier: the S4 arm** (seat ruling 6885452378, ADR-0154 D3 as amended in #33489): a window that starts at or before the newest window a trusted `window` checkpoint names is sealed, so a lagging chain's rows read `late` and unsealed. It also holds an honoured expiry to what it signed: an amendment stored under another chain than its signed organization is a `chain_key` fault, as a checkpoint is, and a checkpoint in an honoured range reads `expired` only within the window the range covers (review 7202871622 M3).
- **verify harness** (`packages/verify/src/harness.ts`, ruling 6884540128 item 4): an `AuditPlugin` that `bootStack` mounts (extra, stack `plugins`, or `requires: ['audit']` provider) adopts `harnessCryptoProvider()`, the instance settings and the engine get; an instance with its own provider keeps it.
- **Docs:** the `lifecycle.seal` describe sentence (and the regenerated `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`), `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` (the sentence at :277, the day alignment, the row budget and tenant windows, plus one line that `sys_audit_log` declares the block), `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (the audit seal lock and `--sealer-stopped` for every run covering the audit log), `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` (the 18.5.0 line now holds on every deployment), `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`.

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.sealed-expiry.test.ts` (new, 11): pending skip and the once-only warning; `archive.keep` plan on both stores and complete-after-delete; `retention.maxAge` per-id engine deletes; `ttl.expireAfter`; a partial guard veto leaves its run uncompleted; a failing plan deletes nothing; slot replacement and disposer; a malformed registration; an unsealed object keeps the row-cutoff path; an archive store with no `bulkDelete` is never planned; a tenant-scoped window travels to the expiry with the column it is set on (review S1, S4, n3).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-expiry-live.integration.test.ts` (new, 10): the real-kernel end-to-end over SQLite with an `archive` datasource. `sys_audit_log` sealed by its own declaration; the plugin's sealer seals; an interrupted expiry (amendment stored, rows still there) reads `expired`; the kernel's own LifecycleService sweep archives, resumes, deletes exactly the expired rows from both stores and then their checkpoints and seeds; a second same-day sweep signs nothing; verify then reads no gap and the untouched windows `unmodified` in hot and in archive; a fully expired chain's next checkpoint links to `last_removed_digest`; `modified`, `missing` and `redacted` are still told apart. A second boot: a sound chain expires whole, a chain stops at a checkpoint no trusted key signed, a chain with a gap is kept, each said once; a stored expiry is never resumed over a checkpoint no trusted key signed (no row and no seed it lists is deleted); a chain head never follows an expiry amendment no trusted key signed (review M1).
- `audit-seal-expiry-window.test.ts` (new, 7): each chain's window — its organization's own where the windows are set on the chain column, the global one, the longest for a chain of no one organization (review S1) and for every chain where the windows are set on another column (S4); and the `policy_change_log` shape over the sealer itself (declared `tenant_id`, injected `organization_id`, the two values differing): windows on `tenant_id` expire each organization's chain under its own window, windows on `organization_id` keep every row to the longest (S4).
- `audit-seal-expiry-admission.test.ts` (new, 14, review 7202871622 M3 and n6, review 7205485052): one pin per check an expiry or the sealer's head makes before it acts — a fresh run's checkpoints bound to the chain and linked, the first linked to the last expiry; a resumed range's checkpoints bound, consecutive, linked, each signature trusted, ending at the amendment's digest, none before its first sequence; a stored expiry bound to the chain; the newest admitted expiry found past more stored ones than one page; and the sealer's head under the same two rules; and a checkpoint whose seed handle names another secret drops nothing but its own row.
- `audit-seal-verifier.test.ts` (+2): an amendment stored under another chain is a `chain_key` fault; a checkpoint whose window ends past its honoured range's `covered_to` is judged, not read `expired` (M3).
- `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts` (+1): the S4 sole-chain window reads `late` unsealed and `ok` false.
- `audit-plugin.test.ts` (+3): the expiry is registered with a crypto provider, unregistered on destroy, not registered without one, and boot survives a lifecycle service without the seam.
- Existing pins adjusted for the seal default (not loosened): `packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.integration.test.ts` and `verify.ownership-queue.integration.test.ts` now expect `sys_audit_log` beside the fixture ledger in `objects` and in the unreachable-archive message, and case 4 reads that a project with no seal of its own still checks the platform's sealed audit log (exit 0); the four `os migrate audit-*` archive and preview integration files (`audit-mail-bodies.archive`, `audit-key-material.archive`, `audit-side-copies.archive`, `preview-read-only`) pass `--sealer-stopped` on their SQLite `--apply` runs (and `preview-read-only`, now judged by the test-source alias gate's source reach, pays its twelve dynamic imports at module top); the two `os migrate audit-*` dogfood files (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/audit-key-material.dogfood.test.ts`, `audit-mail-bodies.dogfood.test.ts`) pass the same flag on their `--apply` runs; and in plugin-audit, `audit-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts` passes `archive: () => 'none'` (its boot connects no archive datasource, as `os audit verify` establishes), and `audit-seal-host-seam-resolve-34280.integration.test.ts` forgets what the loop's own first pass reported before each pin counts its own passes.

## Acceptance notes

- **Rows are kept, never over-deleted, whenever something is off.** No crypto provider, a one-shot boot, a gap, an untrusted checkpoint, a reap guard veto, or a failing plan all keep the rows. A deployment whose `AuditPlugin` has no crypto provider now keeps `sys_audit_log` rows past `archive.keep` instead of pruning them, says so once per process at `warn`, and its sealer reports the missing provider hourly at `error`. An expiry, once run, deletes for good.
- **`os migrate audit-* --apply` on SQLite or Turso now needs `--sealer-stopped`** whenever it rewrites `sys_audit_log`: the 18.6.0 rule for a sealed object (ADR-0154 D3 amended, B, seat ruling 6885005594) now meets every deployment. On Postgres and MySQL every such run now takes the audit seal lock and waits up to ten minutes; dry runs are unchanged. Declared as the narrowing arm with a BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 marker (review M2).
- **The day-aligned cutoff** keeps a row up to one day past its policy, on top of D8's bound, so a drained chain gains at most one expiry amendment a day; amendments are never removed. **10,000 rows a sweep per sealed object**, across its chains; a backlog keeps rows longer, and a cut run continues in the next amendment. Both exceed D8's stated bound in the safe direction; the seat kept them and the add-only ADR-0154 note follows in its own governed PR, beside the skills PR.
- **Tenant-scoped retention windows** apply as the seat ruled on S1 and S4: where the windows are set on the chain column an organization's chain expires under its own window; every other chain under the longest of all, never shorter than a window set for a row in it; each amendment signs the value its chain expired under. The cost: on an object whose windows sit on another column than its chain column, a shorter tenant window has no effect on its sealed rows, which are kept to the longest. `sys_audit_log` itself archives, and `keep` has no override.
- `os audit verify` on a deployment with no `archive` datasource anywhere already reads the hot store alone (`'none'`); a library caller of `verifyAuditLedger` that composes no archive must now pass `archive` for `sys_audit_log`, as the adjusted test does.
- **File surface past the claim:** the two CLI `os audit verify` integration pins, the four CLI `os migrate audit-*` integration files and the two dogfood files above (expectations, the flag and module-top imports only), `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`, `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`, the new `audit-seal-expiry-window.test.ts` and `audit-seal-expiry-admission.test.ts`, `seal-store.testkit.ts` (the in-memory store double judges `$lte`), `packages/verify/vitest.config.ts` (one anchored alias the source-alias gate asks for), `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` and the plugin-audit tenant-audit census page (both regenerated by their own `--write`). Named here for the seat's claim amendment.
- The CLI `os serve` composition is unchanged (it already hands its host provider to `AuditPlugin`, P4b).
- The `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` "not built yet" wording follows in this claim's second PR (Tier H, amendment 7193137455); until then this PR is `Part of #31908`.
- **Small decisions:** the seam is `registerExpiryPrefix` as ruled, and its three types now share that stem (`LifecycleExpiryPrefix`, `LifecycleExpiryPrefixRequest`, `LifecycleExpiryPrefixRun`), so a reader finds them beside the method. A chain of no one organization takes the longest window rather than the global one, the safe reading of the S1 ruling. Under S4 no row is read to pick a window (seat ruling on review 7205485052). Stored expiry amendments are read 50 a page until an admitted one answers, in place of the 10-row scans (review minor). The in-memory store double now judges `$lte`, which the expiry's queries use. A resumed range is read 20 checkpoints a page, as a fresh run is; the chain walk never takes a row with no `chain_key` as its key. These last two have no pin of their own: neither changes a result on a store the platform writes.
- **Owed before queueing:** the delta contract-review-tier L2 over this head (review 7205485052 PASS with S4, S6 and n8–n10 to close), done by the seat.
